scope.output: positive rational finite-support mixture of binomial kernels
explicit_exclusions: downstream AP-time algorithm or hardness consequence

claims.claim: For m=2N, the finite positive Newton truncation has uniform relative error at most 2 exp(-N/40) for all k.
claims.method: finite hypoexponential identity, center-rate stochastic domination, finite Chernoff product and reciprocal-square tail bound

claims.claim: At m=2N, rational Newton coefficients can be computed positive with relative coefficient error epsilon/16 using rational exponential approximations with O(N + log(1/epsilon)) Taylor degree and O(N(N+log(1/epsilon)) log(N+log(1/epsilon))) exponential output bits.
claims.method: Hermite-Genocchi coefficient lower bound, Lagrange cancellation condition <= exp(8N), range reduction and rational Taylor evaluation

claims.claim: The rational beta-kernel polynomial can be represented to relative error epsilon/4 by q=ceil((5N-1)/2) positive rational support atoms, with polynomial bit length and deterministic bit time.
claims.method: exact Gauss-Legendre rule for the polynomial integrand followed by rational root/weight rounding with Markov and algebraic root-separation bounds

claims.claim: Normalizing the positive rational mixture preserves pointwise relative error <= epsilon under the stated regime.
claims.method: positive-entry relative-error transfer through the partition sum

claims.claim: The N125 infinite positive Newton series has a strictly positive explosion defect for every a>0, and the supplied delta=1 Chernoff estimate does not pay the stated generic correction budget.
The N117 contour/Legendre full-separability route is a separate supplied claim and is outside this proof.

finite_evidence.scope: N=1,2,3,4,6,8 high-precision check that positive finite Newton coefficients and rationalized finite Gauss support reproduce the same polynomial populations
finite_evidence.limitation: numeric diagnostic only; does not validate universal bounds, rational Sturm implementation, or source claims
